The Apostle here does not distinguish between prudence and wisdom, though properly it belongs to wisdom to savour spiritual things. Of this spiritual prudence, then, is to be understood that saying of James: [[Jas 3:17|But the wisdom that is from above, first indeed is chaste, then peaceable, modest, easy to be persuaded, consenting to the good|Quæ desursum est sapientia, primum quidem pudica est, deinde pacifica, modesta, suasibilis, bonis consentiens]]. Know too that peace is directly and properly the effect of charity, according to the Psalm: [[Ps 118:165|Much peace have they that love thy law|Pax multa diligentibus legem tuam]]. Peace is also the effect of justice, as removing the hindrances of peace; wherefore it is said through Isaias: [[Is 32:17|And the work of justice shall be peace|Erit opus justitiæ pax]]. Here peace is said to be the effect of prudence, as directing our affections into the way of peace.

paras.t: Quoniam sapientia carnis inimica est Deo, id est divinæ voluntati atque sapientiæ veræ contraria. Ecce nunc loco prudentiæ ponit sapientiam : ex quo certum est, quod inter sapientiam et prudentiam non distinguit. Legi enim Dei non est subjecta sapientia ista carnalis, mundana ac vana, quia nec credit nec agit quæ lex divina tradit esse credenda sive agenda. Propter quod ait Salvator : Confiteor tibi, Pater, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis ; et Jeremias, Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, bene autem facere nescierunt. Nec enim potest divinæ legi esse subjecta sapientia ista. Unum namque oppositorum non subjicitur alteri, sed repugnat. Lex autem divina docet ultimum finem esse constituendum in Deo, hæc vero in bonis carnalibus. Qui autem in carne sunt, id est, carnaliter vivunt, atque in sensibilibus bonis finaliter sistunt, Deo placere non possunt, in quantum hujusmodi. Possunt tamen converti, et Deo reconciliari. Huic dicto consonat illud Salvatoris : Nemo potest duobus dominis servire.
paras.en: [[8:7|Because the wisdom of the flesh is an enemy to God|Quoniam sapientia carnis inimica est Deo]], that is, contrary to the divine will and to true wisdom. See, he now puts wisdom in place of prudence; whence it is certain that he does not distinguish between them. [[8:7|For it is not subject to the law of God|Legi enim Dei non est subjecta]], this carnal, worldly and vain wisdom, because it neither believes nor does what the divine law teaches must be believed or done. Wherefore the Saviour says: [[Luke 10:21|I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hidden these things from the wise and prudent and hast revealed them to little ones|Confiteor tibi, Pater, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis]]; and Jeremias: [[Jer 4:22|they are wise to do evil, but to do good|Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, bene autem facere nescierunt]]. [[8:7|neither can it be|Nec enim potest]] subject to the divine law, this wisdom. For one of two opposites is not subject to the other but resists it. The divine law teaches that the last end is to be placed in God, this wisdom places it in carnal goods. [[8:8|And they who are in the flesh|Qui autem in carne sunt]], that is, who live carnally and rest finally in sensible goods, [[8:8|cannot please God|Deo placere non possunt]], insofar as they are such. Yet they can be converted and reconciled to God. With this saying agrees that of the Saviour: [[Matt 6:24|No man can serve two masters|Nemo potest duobus dominis servire]].

paras.t: Vos autem, o veraciter Christifideles, in carne non estis, id est, in rebus ac vitiis carnis non detinemini, sed spiritualia atque divina exquiritis, conversationem habentes in cœlis, sed in spiritu, id est, in Spiritu Sancto estis, per caritatem et gratiam, et propter spiritualem regenerationem, qua estis ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto renati. Vel, Estis in spiritu vestro, id est secundum rationis judicium vivitis : juxta quod scriptum est, Redite, prævaricatores, ad cor. Si tamen Spiritus Dei, id est Spiritus Sanctus, habitat, id est manet, in vobis per gratiam gratum facientem : quemadmodum loquitur Christus, Ego rogabo Patrem, et alium Paracletum dabit vobis, ut maneat vobiscum in æternum. Rursusque ait : Spiritus Sanctus apud vos manebit, et in vobis erit. Si quis autem Spiritum Christi non habet, id est, cujus anima non habitatur a Spiritu Sancto : qui est Spiritus Christi, quia ab ipso procedit, ab eoque datur ac mittitur, sicut ipse protestatur. Quum venerit Paracletus, quem ego mittam vobis a Patre : et iterum, Ille de meo accipiet. Et ad hoc designandum, insufflavit in discipulos suos, et dixit : Accipite Spiritum Sanctum. Quis autem habet Spiritum Sanctum, nisi quietus et humilis, simplex et justus? Scriptum est enim : Super quem requiescet Spiritus meus, nisi super quietum et humilem? Et iterum : Spiritus Sanctus disciplinæ effugiet fictum, et auferet se a cogitationibus quæ sunt sine intellectu. Hic non est ejus, id est, ad membra Christi non pertinet, secundum præsentem justitiam et merito, quamvis interdum pertineat secundum prædestinationem æternam ac numero, sicut et Paulus quum Stephanum lapidavit.
paras.en: [[8:9|But you are not in the flesh|Vos autem in carne non estis]], O truly faithful of Christ, that is, you are not held fast in the things and vices of the flesh, but seek spiritual and divine things, having your conversation in heaven[[Phil 3:20||]], [[8:9|but the spirit|sed in spiritu]], that is, you are in the Holy Ghost, by charity and grace, and by the spiritual regeneration whereby you are born again of water and the Holy Ghost[[John 3:5||]]. Or, you are in your own spirit, that is, you live according to the judgement of reason, as it is written: [[Is 46:8|return, ye transgressors, to the heart|Redite, prævaricatores, ad cor]]. [[8:9|if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you|Si tamen Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis]], that is, the Holy Ghost abides in you through sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes one pleasing to God]: as Christ says, [[John 14:16|And I will ask the Father: and he shall give you another Paraclete, that he may abide with you for ever|Ego rogabo Patrem, et alium Paracletum dabit vobis, ut maneat vobiscum in æternum]]. And again He says: [[John 14:17|he shall abide with you and shall be in you|apud vos manebit, et in vobis erit]] [Denis supplies “the Holy Ghost” as subject]. [[8:9|Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ|Si quis autem Spiritum Christi non habet]], that is, whose soul is not indwelt by the Holy Ghost, who is the Spirit of Christ because He proceeds from Him and is given and sent by Him, as He Himself declares: [[John 15:26|But when the Paraclete cometh, whom I will send you from the Father|Quum venerit Paracletus, quem ego mittam vobis a Patre]] [the margin gives John xv, 26]; and again: [[John 16:14|he shall receive of mine|Ille de meo accipiet]]. And to signify this He breathed on His disciples and said: [[John 20:22|Receive ye the Holy Ghost|Accipite Spiritum Sanctum]]. But who has the Holy Ghost save the quiet and humble, the simple and just? For it is written: Upon whom shall my Spirit rest, but upon the quiet and the humble?[[Is 66:2||]] [the Vulgate reads differently: “to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little”]. And again: [[Wis 1:5|For the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from the deceitful, and will withdraw himself from thoughts that are without understanding|Spiritus Sanctus disciplinæ effugiet fictum, et auferet se a cogitationibus quæ sunt sine intellectu]]. [[8:9|he is none of his|Hic non est ejus]], that is, he does not belong to the members of Christ according to present justice and by merit, though at times he belongs to them according to eternal predestination and in number, as Paul did when he stoned Stephen[[Acts 7:57||]].

paras.t: Deinde pandit Apostolus, quid utilitatis consequantur fideles ex inhabitatione Spiritus Sancti. Si autem Christus in vobis est, per fidem et caritatem : sicut et alibi legitur, Christum per fidem habitare in cordibus vestris; et Salvator ipse, Ego, inquit, vobiscum sum cunctis diebus ; corpus quidem mortuum est propter peccatum, id est, caro vestra mortalis ac fragilis, necessitati moriendi subjecta est propter originale peccatum, spiritus vero, id est anima vestra, vivit per gratiam, propter justificationem sibi a Christo collatam, id est per hoc quod peccata ei dimissa sunt, quæ spiritum vulnerabant. Vel, Propter justificationem, id est per justitiæ exercitationem. Bona enim operatio, vita est animæ. Hinc ait Salvator : Ego veni ut vitam habeant, et abundantius habeant.
paras.en: Then the Apostle shows what benefit the faithful gain from the indwelling of the Holy Ghost. [[8:10|And if Christ be in you|Si autem Christus in vobis est]] by faith and charity, as is read elsewhere, [[Eph 3:17|That Christ may dwell by faith in your hearts|Christum per fidem habitare in cordibus vestris]]; and the Saviour Himself says, [[Matt 28:20|I am with you all days|Ego … vobiscum sum … diebus]]; [[8:10|the body indeed is dead, because of sin|corpus quidem mortuum est propter peccatum]], that is, your mortal and frail flesh is subject to the necessity of dying because of original sin, [[8:10|but the spirit liveth|spiritus vero vivit]], that is, your soul lives by grace, [[8:10|because of justification|propter justificationem]] conferred on it by Christ, that is, because the sins which wounded the spirit have been forgiven it. Or, because of justification, that is, through the exercise of justice; for good works are the life of the soul. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 10:10|I am come that they may have life and may have it more abundantly|Ego veni ut vitam habeant, et abundantius habeant]].

paras.t: Quod si Spiritus ejus, id est Spiritus Dei Patris, qui suscitavit Jesum Christum a mortuis, habitat in vobis perseveranter usque in finem vitæ præsentis, ita ut in gratia decedatis; qui suscitavit Jesum Christum a mortuis, scilicet Deus Pater, vivificabit, id est, ad immortalem vitam resuscitabit, et mortalia corpora vestra in die novissimo : sicut Job apertissime profitetur : Credo quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum, et rursum circumdabor pelle mea. Per Isaiam quoque Dominus asserit : Vivent mortui tui, interfectique mei resurgent. Propter inhabitantem Spiritum ejus in vobis, id est virtute et gratia Spiritus Sancti; vel, propter benignitatem qua fecit Spiritum Sanctum habitare in mentibus vestris; vel, propter meritum quod consecuti estis ex inhabitatione et gratia Spiritus Sancti : imo, propter utrumque istorum simul, videlicet propter misericordiam Dei et opera vestra bona, suscitabuntur corpora vestra ad beatam et impassibilem vitam.
paras.en: [[8:11|And if the Spirit of him|Quod si Spiritus ejus]], that is, the Spirit of God the Father, [[8:11|that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you|qui suscitavit Jesum a mortuis, habitat in vobis]] perseveringly to the end of the present life, so that you depart in grace; [[8:11|he that raised up Jesus Christ, from the dead|qui suscitavit Jesum Christum a mortuis]], namely God the Father, [[8:11|shall quicken|vivificabit]], that is, shall raise to immortal life, [[8:11|also your mortal bodies|et mortalia corpora vestra]] on the last day: as Job most openly professes: [[Job 19:25|For I know that my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth|Credo quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum]] [[Job 19:26|And I shall be clothed again with my skin|et rursum circumdabor pelle mea]]. Through Isaias also the Lord declares: [[Is 26:19|Thy dead men shall live, my slain shall rise again|Vivent mortui tui, interfectique mei resurgent]]. [[8:11|because of his Spirit that dwelleth in you|propter inhabitantem Spiritum ejus in vobis]], that is, by the power and grace of the Holy Ghost; or, because of the kindness by which He made the Holy Ghost dwell in your minds; or, because of the merit you have gained from the indwelling and grace of the Holy Ghost: nay rather, for both of these together, namely for God's mercy and your good works, your bodies shall be raised to a blessed and impassible life.

paras.t: Ex prædictis infert Apostolus, quod fideles obtemperare tenentur rationi, non sensualitati : spiritui, non carni. Ergo, o fratres, debitores sumus non carni, ut secundum carnem vivamus : id est, quamvis aliquo modo obligemur carni, videlicet ut ei necessaria ministremus in victu atque vestitu, non tamen sic ei obligati sumus, ut ejus concupiscentiis acquiescamus, carnaliterque vivamus. Si enim secundum carnem vixeritis, moriemini, morte culpæ in hoc sæculo, et morte perpetua in inferno. Si autem spiritu, id est gratia Spiritus Sancti; vel, Spiritu, id est rationis vestræ judicio ; facta, id est opera, carnis mortificaveritis, id est, destruxeritis et abjeceritis tanquam venena : quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico præcipitur, Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccatum ; vivetis, vita caritatis et gratiæ in Ecclesia militanti, vita quoque fruitionis et gloriæ in Ecclesia triumphanti. Huic documento naturalis consonat ratio. Media namque disponenda sunt secundum exigentiam finis. Quum ergo caro sit animæ instrumentum, et ordinetur ad spiritum sicut ad finem, regenda est secundum exigentiam animæ seu spiritus, scilicet, ut animæ serviat, rationi obediat, illisque actibus occupetur per quæ spiritus tendit et redit ad Creatorem. Qui autem secundum carnem conversatur, pervertit hunc ordinem, dominam ancillæ subjiciens, finem medio postponens, et se ipsum bestiis viliorem ac deteriorem constituens.
paras.en: From the foregoing the Apostle infers that the faithful are bound to obey reason, not sensuality; the spirit, not the flesh. [[8:12|Therefore, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh to live according to the flesh|Ergo, o fratres, debitores sumus non carni, ut secundum carnem vivamus]]: that is, though we are in some way bound to the flesh, namely to supply it what it needs in food and clothing, yet we are not so bound to it as to yield to its concupiscences and live carnally. [[8:13|For if you live according to the flesh, you shall die|Si enim secundum carnem vixeritis, moriemini]], by the death of guilt in this world and by everlasting death in hell. [[8:13|but if by the Spirit|Si autem spiritu]], that is, by the grace of the Holy Ghost; or, by the spirit, that is, by the judgement of your reason, [[8:13|you mortify the deeds of the flesh|facta carnis mortificaveritis]], that is, the works, destroy them and cast them off as poisons: as is commanded in Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 21:2|Flee from sins as from the face of a serpent|Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccatum]]; [[8:13|you shall live|vivetis]], the life of charity and grace in the Church militant, and the life of fruition and glory in the Church triumphant. Natural reason agrees with this teaching. For means must be ordered as the end requires. Since then the flesh is the instrument of the soul and is ordered to the spirit as to its end, it must be ruled as the soul or spirit requires: that it serve the soul, obey reason, and be occupied in those acts by which the spirit tends and returns to its Creator. But he who lives according to the flesh perverts this order, subjecting the mistress to the handmaid, putting the end after the means, and making himself viler and worse than the beasts.

paras.t: Quicumque enim Spiritu Dei aguntur, id est, a Spiritu Sancto reguntur, ejus instinctu ducuntur, ejus fervore impelluntur ad bona, hi sunt filii Dei, per gratiam adoptantem ac filialem amorem. Unde in Canonica Joannis scribitur : Videte qualem caritatem dedit nobis Deus Pater, ut filii Dei nominemur et simus. Quemadmodum autem Deus omnipotens movet ceteras creaturas ad proprias operationes, naturalemque finem, per quemdam universalem influxum seu generalem gubernationem (secundum quod Proclus auctor libri de Causis affirmat : Causa prima regit res omnes, præterquam quod commisceatur eis) ; sic rationalem creaturam movet ad finem supernaturalem per specialem gubernationem ac inspirationem, quæ providentia appellatur. Electos vero singulariter movet ac regit, providens eis non solum sufficienter, sed etiam efficaciter, de omnibus necessariis ad salutem, ita ut gratiam Dei suscipiant, ejusque inspirationi acquiescant. Idcirco dicuntur potius agi, quam regi vel moveri a Spiritu Sancto, ut magnitudo gratiæ insinuetur. Ad actum enim meritorium, non solum exigitur gratia habitualis, sed insuper necessaria est quædam actualis motio Spiritus Sancti voluntatem excitantis. Propter quod Propheta dicebat : Domine, omnia opera nostra operatus es in nobis. — Porro, quum motio ista sive influxus, actio et instinctus Spiritus Sancti, sit penitus supernaturalis, indiget anima supernaturalibus quibusdam habitibus, per quos aptetur ac disponatur ad hujus motionis facilem susceptionem. Hi vero habitus, sunt septem dona Spiritus Sancti, quæ sunt dispositiones habituales ac supernaturales, a Deo immediate per creationem infusæ, quibus redditur anima facile mobilis a Spiritu Sancto in ordine ad supernaturalem finem, quæ est vita æterna. Hæc dona a virtutibus realiter distinguuntur, easque in dignitate excedunt, theologicis demptis virtutibus. Per hæc dona dirigitur anima a Spiritu Sancto, ita ut audiat eum sicut magistrum. Unde ait Psalmista : Spiritus tuus bonus deducet me in terram rectam. — Qui itaque sic aguntur Spiritu Dei, hi sunt filii Dei. Quicumque autem in gratia est, habet hæc dona secundum aliquem gradum, et agitur a Spiritu Sancto quantum requirit status salutis, videlicet ad observantiam præceptorum.
paras.en: [[8:14|For whosoever are led by the Spirit of God|Quicumque enim Spiritu Dei aguntur]], that is, are ruled by the Holy Ghost, led by His prompting, driven to good things by His fervour, [[8:14|they are the sons of God|hi sunt filii Dei]], by adopting grace and filial love. Hence it is written in the Canonical Epistle of John: [[1 John 3:1|Behold what manner of charity the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called and should be|Videte qualem caritatem dedit nobis Deus Pater, ut filii Dei nominemur et simus]]. Now as almighty God moves the other creatures to their proper operations and natural end by a certain universal influence or general government (as Proclus, the author of the book *On Causes*, affirms: The first cause rules all things without being mingled with them), so He moves the rational creature to its supernatural end by a special government and inspiration, which is called providence. And the elect He moves and rules singularly, providing them not only sufficiently but also efficaciously with all things necessary to salvation, so that they receive God's grace and yield to His inspiration. Therefore they are said rather to be *driven* [Latin *agi*, rendered “led” in the Douay] than ruled or moved by the Holy Ghost, to suggest the greatness of grace. For a meritorious act requires not only habitual grace, but also a certain actual motion of the Holy Ghost stirring the will. Wherefore the Prophet said: [[Is 26:12|Lord, thou wilt give us peace: for thou hast wrought all our works for us|Domine … omnia … opera nostra operatus es nobis]]. — Further, since this motion or influence, action and prompting of the Holy Ghost is wholly supernatural, the soul needs certain supernatural habits by which it is fitted and disposed to receive this motion readily. These habits are the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]], which are habitual and supernatural dispositions infused by God immediately by creation, whereby the soul is made readily movable by the Holy Ghost towards its supernatural end, which is life everlasting. These gifts are really distinct from the virtues and excel them in dignity, the theological virtues excepted. By these gifts the soul is directed by the Holy Ghost, so that it hears Him as a master. Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 142:10|Thy good spirit shall lead me into the right land|Spiritus tuus bonus deducet me in terram rectam]]. — Those, then, who are thus led by the Spirit of God are the sons of God. And whoever is in grace has these gifts in some degree, and is led by the Holy Ghost as far as the state of salvation requires, namely to the keeping of the commandments.

paras.t: Deinde ponitur ratio cur morituri simus, si secundum carnem vixerimus. Non enim accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore, id est, jam tempore gratiæ, non est vobis datus spiritus quo serviatis Deo serviliter quasi invite, videlicet timore pœnarum, ut olim tempore legis, quæ comminatione pœnarum induxit homines ad serviendum ; sed accepistis spiritum adoptionis filiorum Dei, id est spiritum cujus gratia homines adoptantur in filios Dei, in quo clamamus ore vel corde : Abba (Pater). Duo sunt nomina, unum Hebraeum, alterum Latinum, significantia idem. Et est sensus : In hoc spiritu vocamus ex caritate, tanquam filii adoptivi, Deum Patrem fiducialiter atque affectuose, dicentes : Pater noster qui es in cœlis.
paras.en: Next is given the reason why we shall die if we live according to the flesh. [[8:15|For you have not received the spirit of bondage again in fear|Non enim accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore]], that is, now in the time of grace there has not been given you a spirit by which you serve God servilely, as it were unwillingly, namely through fear of punishment, as formerly in the time of the law, which by threat of punishment brought men to serve[[Deut 28:15||]]; [[8:15|but you have received the spirit of adoption of sons|sed accepistis spiritum adoptionis filiorum]] of God, that is, the spirit by whose grace men are adopted as sons of God, [[8:15|whereby we cry|in quo clamamus]] with mouth or heart: [[8:15|Abba (Father)|Abba (Pater)]]. These are two names, one Hebrew, the other Latin, meaning the same. And the sense is: In this spirit we call upon God the Father out of charity, as adopted sons, confidently and lovingly, saying: [[Matt 6:9|Our Father who art in heaven|Pater noster qui es in cœlis]].

paras.t: Glossa per spiritum servitutis, intelligit Spiritum Sanctum, a quo cordibus Judæorum incussus est timor pœnarum, quo serviliter servierunt. Nam et timor servilis, in quantum est timor, a Spiritu Sancto est. Sic enim retrahit a peccato et disponit ad gratiam. Quantum vero ad servilitatem suam, nec bonus est, neque a Spiritu Sancto. Dicitur ergo Spiritus Sanctus, spiritus servitutis, ratione sui effectus, quia facit servire. Quantum ad hoc, receperunt [eum] qui ejus dono gratis dato servierunt timore pœnarum. Per spiritum vero adoptionis, intelligit Glossa eumdem Spiritum Sanctum per gratiam adoptantem. Unde Augustinus : Cave, inquit, ne ex eo quod ait, Spiritum servitutis, et, Spiritum adoptionis, diversum intelligas spiritum, quum sit unus atque idem Spiritus, qui in Trinitate dicitur Spiritus Sanctus : quod etiam Apostolus ostendit, dicens, Iterum. Sed propter diversa opera dissimiliter nominatur. Huic dicto concordat quod de Spiritu subditur, Ipse enim Spiritus testimonium reddit spiritui nostro, quod sumus filii Dei : quod certum est dici de Spiritu Sancto, videturque dictum de eodem spiritu de quo nunc agitur.
paras.en: The Gloss understands by the spirit of bondage the Holy Ghost, by whom the fear of punishment was struck into the hearts of the Jews, through which they served servilely. For servile fear too, insofar as it is fear, is from the Holy Ghost; for thus it draws back from sin and disposes to grace. But as to its servility, it is neither good nor from the Holy Ghost. The Holy Ghost, then, is called the spirit of bondage by reason of His effect, because He makes men serve. In this respect they received Him who, by His gift freely given [*gratis datum*, a grace given for others' good or without sanctifying], served through fear of punishment. By the spirit of adoption the Gloss understands the same Holy Ghost adopting through grace. Hence Augustine says: Beware lest, from his saying “the spirit of bondage” and “the spirit of adoption”, you understand a different spirit, since it is one and the same Spirit who in the Trinity is called the Holy Ghost: which the Apostle also shows by saying “again”. But because of different works He is named differently. With this agrees what is added of the Spirit: [[8:16|For the Spirit himself giveth testimony to our spirit that we are the sons of God|Ipse enim Spiritus testimonium reddit spiritui nostro, quod sumus filii Dei]]: which is certainly said of the Holy Ghost, and seems said of the same spirit now treated.

paras.t: Quidam vero per spiritum intelligunt donum Spiritus Sancti : ut spiritus adoptionis dicatur donum filialis timoris, qui nos efficit filios Dei; spiritus vero servitutis intelligatur donum timoris servilis, videlicet ipse timor servilis. Hæc enim, secundum Augustinum, est brevis differentia legis et Evangelii : timor et amor. Lex vetus appellata est lex timoris, quoniam comminatione pœnarum induxit ad bonum, nec præstitit gratiam obediendi per caritatem. Porro lex evangelica, est lex amoris : agit enim, gratiam conferendo, servire Deo amore justitiæ. Non est autem sic intelligendum, quin multi in veteri Testamento acceperunt spiritum adoptionis filiorum Dei. Omnes enim electi habuerunt hunc spiritum, sed non ex lege, neque per legem, magis autem ex Deo per fidem qua crediderunt in Christum venturum, ad cujus gratiam confugerunt, legis insufficientiam cognoscentes, propriamque infirmitatem pensantes.
paras.en: Some, however, understand by spirit a gift of the Holy Ghost: so that the spirit of adoption is the gift of filial fear, which makes us sons of God, and the spirit of bondage is the gift of servile fear, namely servile fear itself. For this, according to Augustine, is the brief difference between the Law and the Gospel: fear and love. The old law was called the law of fear because it led to good by threat of punishment and did not give the grace of obeying through charity. But the Gospel law is the law of love: for by conferring grace it makes men serve God out of love of justice. Yet this is not to be understood as though many in the Old Testament did not receive the spirit of adoption of the sons of God. For all the elect had this spirit, but not from the law nor through the law, but rather from God, through the faith by which they believed in Christ to come, to whose grace they fled, knowing the insufficiency of the law and weighing their own weakness.

paras.t: Videtur quoque per spiritum hoc loco posse intelligi spiritus rationalis creatus, videlicet anima nostra. Quamvis autem quilibet nostrum acceperit hunc spiritum suum, quando creata corporique infusa est anima sua, dicimur tamen spiritum istum recipere vel amittere, quando aliqua nova dispositio ei confertur vel aufertur, quemadmodum aliquis dicitur concipere spiritum devotum, vel perdere animam ferventem. Juxta quem sensum Dominus ait : Auferam cor lapideum de carne vestra, et dabo vobis cor carneum. Qui ergo sub lege servierunt timore, accepisse dicuntur spiritum servitutis, id est animam servientem in timore. Qui vero sub gratia serviunt caritate, accipiunt spiritum adoptionis, id est animam habentem gratiam adoptionis : in quo spiritu clamant corde devoto, Abba (Pater). Huic vero consonat quod alibi ait Apostolus : Non dedit nobis Deus spiritum timoris, sed virtutis et dilectionis.
paras.en: It seems too that by spirit in this place may be understood the created rational spirit, namely our soul. Although each of us received this his spirit when his soul was created and infused into the body, we are yet said to receive or lose this spirit when some new disposition is conferred on it or taken from it, as one is said to conceive a devout spirit or to lose a fervent soul. In which sense the Lord says: [[Ezech 36:26|I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and will give you a heart of flesh|Auferam cor lapideum de carne vestra, et dabo vobis cor carneum]]. Those, then, who under the law served in fear are said to have received the spirit of bondage, that is, a soul serving in fear. But those who under grace serve in charity receive the spirit of adoption, that is, a soul having the grace of adoption: in which spirit they cry with devout heart, Abba (Father). With this agrees what the Apostle says elsewhere: [[2 Tim 1:7|For God hath not given us the spirit of fear: but of power and of love|Non dedit nobis Deus spiritum timoris, sed virtutis et dilectionis]].

paras.t: Quod autem in Spiritu Sancto clamemus, Abba (Pater), et Deum vere Patrem vocemus, hinc constat : Ipse enim Spiritus Sanctus testimonium reddit spiritui nostro, id est, testificatur animæ nostræ, eamque recognoscere facit per inspirationem internam, vel revelationem apertam, quod sumus filii Dei adoptivi, stando in caritate et gratia.
paras.en: That we cry in the Holy Ghost, Abba (Father), and truly call God Father, is clear from this: [[8:16|For the Spirit himself giveth testimony to our spirit|Ipse enim Spiritus Sanctus testimonium reddit spiritui nostro]] (the Holy Ghost), that is, testifies to our soul and makes it recognize, by inward inspiration or open revelation, [[8:16|that we are the sons of God|quod sumus filii Dei]] by adoption, while we stand in charity and grace.

paras.t: Testificatio ista multis modis intelligi potest. Primo, per manifestam et claram revelationem Spiritus Sancti, sive fiat immediate ab ipso, sive per angelum : sicque agnoscit homo per certitudinem se esse in gratia et filiatione divina, sicut Paulus et ceteri Apostoli, imo et multi perfecti ita sciverunt se esse in gratia. Ad quos maxime pertinet quod alio loco dicit Apostolus : Nos non spiritum hujus mundi accepimus, sed spiritum qui ex Deo est, ut sciamus quæ a Deo donata sunt nobis. Hoc modo agnovit Abraham se esse filium Dei, quum ei Dominus promisit quod decederet in senectute bona. Ezechias quoque certissime dixit : Memento, Domine, quomodo ambulaverim coram te in veritate et in corde perfecto. Secundo, fit testificatio ista per quamdam bonæ fiduciæ consolatoriam infusionem : ut quum homo nimium anxiatur an placeat Deo, et subito sentit se consolari et quasi certificari. Sic autem omnes virtuosi et boni scire possunt se esse filios Dei, non quidem certo, sed conjecturaliter et probabiliter. Tertio, fit per propriæ conversationis et conscientiæ diligentem discussionem : ut quum homo non habet remorsum mortalis peccati, et cum debita diligentia custodit mandata, auditque verbum Dei libenter. Ista sunt probabilia signa filiationis divinæ, imo et prædestinationis, secundum quod ait Salvator : Qui ex Deo est, verba Dei audit; et Joannes in sua Canonica, Si cor nostrum non reprehenderit nos, fiduciam habemus ad Deum ; et rursus, Qui servat verbum Christi, vere in hoc caritas Dei perfecta est. — Denique, sicut vita naturæ cognoscitur ex vitalibus actibus ac naturalibus motibus animæ, sic vita gratiæ ex bonis operibus, seu mandatorum custodia comprobatur, quia ut Gregorius ait, Exhibitio operis, probatio est caritatis. Quum ergo Spiritus Sanctus facit nos bene agere, atque in Dei obsequio promptos et agiles esse, tunc utique testimonium perhibet spiritui nostro, quod filii Dei simus.
paras.en: This testimony can be understood in many ways. First, by a manifest and clear revelation of the Holy Ghost, whether made immediately by Him or through an angel: and so a man knows with certainty that he is in grace and divine sonship, as Paul and the other Apostles, and indeed many perfect souls, thus knew themselves to be in grace. To these chiefly belongs what the Apostle says in another place: [[1 Cor 2:12|Now, we have received not the spirit of this world, but the Spirit that is of God: that we may know the things that are given us from God|Nos non spiritum hujus mundi accepimus, sed spiritum qui ex Deo est, ut sciamus quæ a Deo donata sunt nobis]]. In this way Abraham knew himself to be a son of God, when the Lord promised him that he should die in a good old age[[Gen 15:15||]]. Ezechias also most certainly said: [[4 Kings 20:3|remember how I have walked before thee in truth, and with a perfect heart|Memento, Domine, quomodo ambulaverim coram te in veritate et in corde perfecto]]. Secondly, this testimony is given by a consoling infusion of good confidence: as when a man is greatly anxious whether he pleases God, and suddenly feels himself consoled and as it were assured. In this way all virtuous and good men can know that they are sons of God, not indeed with certainty, but by conjecture and probably. Thirdly, it is given through diligent examination of one's own conduct and conscience: as when a man has no remorse of mortal sin, keeps the commandments with due diligence, and gladly hears the word of God. These are probable signs of divine sonship, and even of predestination, as the Saviour says: [[John 8:47|He that is of God heareth the words of God|Qui ex Deo est, verba Dei audit]]; and John in his Canonical Epistle: [[1 John 3:21|if our heart do not reprehend us, we have confidence towards God|Si cor nostrum non reprehenderit nos, fiduciam habemus ad Deum]]; and again: [[1 John 2:5|But he that keepeth his word, in him in very deed the charity of God is perfected|Qui servat verbum Christi, vere in hoc caritas Dei perfecta est]]. — Lastly, as the life of nature is known from the vital acts and natural movements of the soul, so the life of grace is proved by good works, or the keeping of the commandments; for, as Gregory says, the showing of the work is the proof of love. When therefore the Holy Ghost makes us act well and be prompt and nimble in God's service, then indeed He bears witness to our spirit that we are sons of God.

paras.t: Huic ergo dicto Apostoli non repugnat quod scriptum est : Sunt justi atque sapientes, et opera eorum in manu Dei sunt ; et tamen nescit homo utrum amore an odio dignus sit, sed omnia in futurum servantur incerta. Et quod ait beatus Job : Si venerit ad me, non videbo eum, et si recesserit a me, non intelligam ; itemque, Si simplex fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea. Hæc enim atque similia ideo asseruntur, quia de lege communi et humano processu seu via, non potest homo agnoscere per certitudinem se esse filium Dei per gratiæ adoptionem. Postremo, melius atque facilius potest quis scire se esse in gratia et esse filium Dei secundum præsentem justitiam, quam esse prædestinatum, vel in gratia permansurum. Unde hoc certo agnosci non potest, nisi per revelationem divinam.
paras.en: This saying of the Apostle, then, is not contradicted by what is written: [[Eccles 9:1|there are just men and wise men, and their works are in the hand of God|Sunt justi atque sapientes, et opera eorum in manu Dei sunt]]: and yet [[Eccles 9:1|man knoweth not whether he be worthy of love, or hatred|nescit homo utrum amore an odio dignus sit]], [[Eccles 9:2|But all things are kept uncertain|sed omnia in futurum servantur incerta]]. Nor by what blessed Job says: [[Job 9:11|If he come to me, I shall not see him: if he depart, I shall not understand|Si venerit ad me, non videbo eum, et si recesserit a me, non intelligam]]; and likewise: [[Job 9:21|Although I should be simple, even this my soul shall be ignorant of|Si simplex fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea]]. For these and like things are asserted because by the common law and the human course or way a man cannot know with certainty that he is a son of God by the adoption of grace. Finally, one can know better and more easily that he is in grace and a son of God according to present justice than that he is predestined or will persevere in grace. This latter cannot be known with certainty except by divine revelation.

paras.t: Si autem filii Dei jam sumus per gratiam adoptantem, et heredes erimus in patria per gloriam beatificantem. Filiis enim adoptivis debetur aliqua pars hereditatis paternæ. Erimus autem heredes quidem, non cujuscumque, sed Dei, æternaliter possidendo bona Domini in terra viventium, quæ oculus non vidit nec auris audivit. Maxime tamen ista Beatorum hereditas est ipsa Divinitas, quæ est objectalis beatitudo indivisibilis in se : quæ tota habetur a singulis, a nullo autem totaliter, et ita dividitur secundum quod diversimode participatur : quæ diversitas est ex parte recipientium, quorum unus alio clarius conspicit Deum. De hac hereditate fertur in Psalmo : Dominus pars hereditatis meæ ; et, Satiabor quum apparuerit gloria tua. Per Isaiam quoque Dominus loquitur : Sustollam te super altitudinem terræ, et cibabo te hereditate patris tui Jacob. Ceteræ hereditates terminantur in morte. Hæc autem a morte sumit exordium, juxta illud : Quum dederit dilectis suis somnum, ecce hereditas Domini. Coheredes autem Christi, id est, beatitudinis Christi consortes atque participes erimus. Ipse est enim principalis heres, et nos simul cum ipso divinam beatitudinem consequemur. Quo autem merito, subditur : si tamen compatimur, id est, Christi passionibus configuremur, bajulando crucem nostram, et sequendo vestigia ejus : ad hunc finem, ut et simul glorificemur, id est, gloriosi efficiamur cum Christo glorificato, quemadmodum ipse profitetur : Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi sum ego, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem meam.
paras.en: [[8:17|And if sons|Si autem filii]] of God we now are by adopting grace, [[8:17|heirs also|et hæredes]] we shall be in the fatherland by beatifying glory. For to adopted sons some part of the father's inheritance is due. And we shall be [[8:17|heirs indeed of God|hæredes, quidem Dei]], not of anyone at all, but of God, possessing eternally the good things of the Lord in the land of the living[[Ps 26:13||]], which [[1 Cor 2:9|Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard|oculus non vidit nec auris audivit]]. But above all this inheritance of the Blessed is the Godhead itself, which is the objective beatitude, indivisible in itself: which is had wholly by each, but by none totally [that is, each possesses the whole God, but none comprehends Him fully], and so is divided according as it is shared in diverse ways; which diversity is on the part of the receivers, one of whom sees God more clearly than another. Of this inheritance it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 15:5|The Lord is the portion of my inheritance|Dominus pars hereditatis meæ]]; and: [[Ps 16:15|I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear|Satiabor quum apparuerit gloria tua]]. Through Isaias also the Lord says: [[Is 58:14|I will lift thee up above the high places of the earth, and will feed thee with the inheritance of Jacob thy father|Sustollam te super altitudinem terræ, et cibabo te hereditate patris tui Jacob]] [the margin gives Is. lviii, 14]. Other inheritances end at death; but this one takes its beginning from death, according to that: [[Ps 126:2|When he shall give sleep|Quum dederit dilectis suis somnum]], [[Ps 126:3|Behold the inheritance of the Lord|ecce hereditas Domini]]. [[8:17|and joint heirs with Christ|cohæredes autem Christi]], that is, we shall be sharers and partakers of Christ's beatitude. For He is the principal heir, and we together with Him shall attain the divine beatitude. And by what merit is added: [[8:17|if we suffer with him|si tamen compatimur]], that is, if we are conformed to the sufferings of Christ, carrying our cross[[Matt 16:24||]][[Luke 14:27||]] and following in His footsteps: to this end, [[8:17|that we may be also glorified with him|ut et conglorificemur]] [Denis divides it, *simul glorificemur*], that is, be made glorious with Christ glorified, as He Himself declares: [[John 17:24|Father, I will that where I am, they also whom thou hast given me may be with me: that they may see my glory|Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi sum ego, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem meam]].
